| ASF-1 | the shipped provenance log does not reproduce under the code shipped beside it; all five replayable records mismatch | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — The screen is the general one and it is cheap: re-run the record from its own fields and diff. It needs no domain knowledge and asks the question a provenance format exists to answer. The decisive detail is that record db001b18502f reproduces fixation_probability EXACTLY (0.65/0.35/0.0) and disagrees only on the timing fields -- so this is the same dynamics code with something changed around it, not a log of a different experiment. Mechanised as --verify, and the record now carries code_sha256 and a content-addressed run_id. |
| ASF-10 | fluctuating_fixation is a claim about the step budget; sweeping num_steps alone flips the verdict at fixed biology | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **NULL_ARTIFACT** — Right-censoring reported as a biological outcome. The screen generalises past this model: vary the simulation's own resource with the physics held fixed and see whether the verdict moves. Measured, every 'coexisting' replicate is exactly a censored one -- the two fractions are equal to floating point -- which is the cheapest possible diagnostic and was one line away the whole time. |
| ASF-11 | switching_rate is a continuous-time generator rate consumed as a per-step Bernoulli probability, so it saturates at 1.0 | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **UNITS** — Rates 2.0, 5.0 and 50.0 give byte-identical outcomes. The compounding part is the reusable warning: the agent's exploration branch multiplies the rate by 1.3, so it walks into the saturated region in seven steps from the shipped default and keeps exploring a knob that has stopped responding. Not patched -- fixing it means choosing a time discretisation, which is modelling. |
| ASF-12 | the competition radius was derived from dispersal_range, so dispersal_range 1 disables competition entirely while competition_strength stays logged nonzero | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — One knob driving two mechanisms, and the agent can reach the value that silently switches one of them off. The fix that costs nothing is to make the derived quantity an explicit parameter defaulting to the old expression: behaviour unchanged, confound nameable. Reusable as a sweep -- take the shared knob to its extreme and check the second mechanism is still on. |
| ASF-13 | exploration_rate was stored and never read; 0.0 and 1.0 gave identical behaviour | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — The third instance of the unread-parameter shape after GR-2's bands_per_octave and GLY-3's sub_glyphs, and the detector is the same two-line sweep: run at both extremes and diff. Cheap enough to run over every declared parameter in a module, which is the mechanisation nothing has yet. |
| ASF-14 | forest_species_coexistence returns the same verdict for competitive exclusion and for an empty grid | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — Measured over 5 seeds at every setting the agent can reach, richness is 3,3,3,3,3; the only configuration that fails the claim is high mortality, where richness is 0 because the forest is dead. So the claim's one reachable failure mode is not the one it is named for. The remedy reuses ASF-5's inconclusive channel rather than inventing a coexistence threshold, which would have been a claim about forests. |
| ASF-15 | the auto-generated claim's description asserted a correlation with seed_rate that its single-run threshold test never varied | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **UNFALSIFIABLE** — Two defects in one line and only the second is interesting: the description names a correlation nothing sweeps, and the threshold is written in the density-exponent convention while the tested quantity is a binned-count slope (ASF-9), so it fails on arrival at the observed slopes. Correcting the description was right; testing the correlation needs a sweep the loop cannot express, which is open problem ASF-A. |
| ASF-16 | claim ids embedded int(time.time()), so two claims generated in the same second collide | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — Minor and measured rather than argued: generating two claims in a loop produces one id. Kept because a collision in an id namespace makes the claim history unreadable in exactly the place ASF-4 already made it empty. |
| ASF-2 | the record's random_seed was never passed to any seeding call, so forest iterations k>0 were unreplayable | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — A seed field that is written but never passed to a seeding call reads as reproducibility and supplies none -- and the model that WAS replayable was replayable through base_seed, the field not named seed. Worth keeping: base_seed being held fixed across iterations is correct and deliberate, because it makes successive iterations a paired comparison; it was right by accident and now says so. |
| ASF-3 | iteration_results paired each iteration's outcomes with the next iteration's parameters | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — The jsonl was correct and the in-memory structure was shifted by one, so the two authorities disagreed and only the one nobody plots was right. The tail coincides -- the final iteration does not call the agent -- which is how an off-by-one survives a glance at the end of the output. The check is to compare a parameter that actually MOVES; against a static one the assertion passes without testing anything. |
| ASF-4 | log_claim_result had no callers, so claims_tested was empty on every run | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — A summary field that is always empty is indistinguishable from a system that tested nothing, and neither the summary nor the tests noticed. Cheap general form: for every accumulator a summary reports, grep for a caller. |
| ASF-5 | a raising test function was recorded as a refutation; the inconclusive status was created and discarded one line later | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — The distinction between 'measured and failed' and 'could not measure' was already in the code and was thrown away at the record boundary -- so the fix was to propagate a state that already existed, not to invent one. Reachable on the shipped defaults: the forest test formats 'N/A' with :.3f, so a collapsed forest was logged as a refuted power law. The same shape appeared in the verifier written to catch it, where a replay that raised left diffs empty and read as a clean reproduction. |
| ASF-6 | the agent's num_steps branch was unreachable: one hypothesis string contained both substrings and the other was tested first | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — The reusable form is the reachability sweep over a system's own diagnosis set -- take every diagnosis it can emit and confirm each changes something. Mechanised for this system in tests/test_adaptive_sim.py::test_every_diagnosis_tag_reaches_an_action. Also the strongest argument in the archive for not branching on generated prose: the shipped fluctuating log shows four iterations spent on one knob at a pinned outcome, and the run that worked raised num_steps by hand, out of band. |
| ASF-7 | fed a near-extinct forest, the agent proposes increasing competition strength | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **CODE_ERROR** — ASF-5 and ASF-6 compound into a wrong action, which is the reason to care about either: the response to a dying forest is to kill it harder, recorded as a hypothesis under test. An audit that stopped at 'the exception handling is untidy' would not have reached it. |
| ASF-8 | forest_power_law constrains the straightness of a log-log fit and not the sign of the slope; uniform[1,1000] passes 100% of draws at slope +0.919 | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **NULL_ARTIFACT** — The measured pass rates are the reusable part, and the useful subtlety is that the gate is NOT vacuous -- it rejects exponential and gamma at 0% while passing uniform and lognormal at 100%. 'R2 is meaningless on log-binned data' would have been the easy verdict and it is wrong; the defect is specifically that nothing constrains the slope. Not patched: choosing a slope constraint is a claim about forests. |
| ASF-9 | the log-binned histogram is not divided by bin width, so the fitted slope estimates 1-alpha rather than -alpha | live | refutation | FALSIFIER | **MATH_ERROR** — The arithmetic is exact and reusable: with logarithmic bins the count carries a factor of the bin width, so slope = 1 - alpha. Verified at alpha 1.5/2.0/2.5/3.0 giving -0.473/-0.944/-1.442/-1.900. Consequence worth carrying: the shipped slopes of -0.369 and -0.412 are density exponents near 1.4, and a self-thinning -2 would appear here as -1, so any threshold written in the density convention is off by one. |
